runs.text: It is hard for many to comprehend how God can love them as sinners. As a result, most people are running away from God out of fear. This is one way the devil veils the good news of the gospel. For this reason, it is important to realize that the basis for our salvation is God’s love for us and the gift of His Son. Salvation is not based on our own goodness. It is a gift. Jesus Himself declared in John 3:16:
“God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whoever believes in Him shall not perish but have everlasting life”
The Apostle Paul, once a persecutor of the Christian church, made this profound statement to young Timothy:
“This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.”
(1 Timothy 1:15)
The reason why we sinners do not need to be afraid of God is that
God is love.
Once our eyes are opened to this fact, the gospel will become fantastic, or incredibly good news. Let us see how this is true from the Word of God.
GOD’S LOVE:
1. How does God demonstrate His love?
John 3:16
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
Note:

The world that God so loved is the world that had rebelled against Him. Therefore, we are saved not because we deserve it, but because God is love. God gave His Son at infinite loss to Himself. This is the foundation of a correct understanding of the gospel. It is because of the gift of His only begotten Son, that we can see that God is love, and we can then return this love back to Him.
2. After Paul shows that all are sinners deserving God’s wrath, what reason does he give that God redeemed humanity in Christ?
Ephesians 2:4
But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us
, 5 Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved.) 6 And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus.
Note:
Even though the Bible declares that we are all sinners, it also tells us that God loves us infinitely. That is why “
God made us alive together with Christ, raised us up together, and made us sit in heavenly places in Him
”. All because of His love for each member of the human family.
3. Since we are not saved by works of righteousness or right doing, why did God save us?
Titus 3:3
For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another. 4
But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared,
Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us
, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost.
Note:
The basis for our salvation rests upon God’s love and mercy for sinners. Scripture declares that “
God is love
” (1 John 4:8). This love is not just one of God’s characteristics but it is what He is by His very nature.
4. How far-reaching is God’s love?
Matthew 5:45
That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven:
for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust
Note:

God’s love extends beyond all barriers, and is the opposite of human love. God even loves and cares for those who are His enemies by supplying all their needs. God’s love does not depend on our goodness. Therefore, in understanding God’s love for us, we must never attribute our human concepts of love to God. This is where many go wrong.
5. What is the foundation for our love for God?
1 John 4:10
Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that He loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins
Note:

The basis for our love for God is not that we love Him, but that God loves us. God demonstrated His endearing love for mankind by sending the very best gift that He had in His treasury. God demonstrated His love for mankind by sending His only begotten Son. Take some time to contemplate this love. The God of the universe sent His only Son to save a race that had become His enemy! (See Question #6)
6. What were we when Christ died for us?
Romans 5:8
But God commendeth his love toward us, in that,
while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us
. 9 Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. 10 For if,
when we were enemies
we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son
, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.
Note:

This passage tells us that while we were enemies of God, He redeemed us through the death of His Son. Such love is beyond our comprehension, but it is real because God says so, and He demonstrated it in the sacrifice of His Son.
7. What draws us to God?
Jeremiah 31:3
The LORD hath appeared of old unto me, saying,
Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.
Note:

Most people are running away from God because they think He is out to punish them. But the truth is that God loves us and gave us His only Son so that whosoever believes in Him should not be lost, but have everlasting life. This is what draws us to God.
8. What endearing term does God use for His people?
1 John 3:1
Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God:

therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not. 2 Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.
Note:

Many deceptions have come into the world that prevent us from seeing Christ as He is! What is He? Jesus is the Son of God. We need to break through these barriers and see the love of the Father in the gift of His Son!

When we see our Father’s tender love for us, it changes us. God’s self-sacrificing love then spills over into our lives as we contemplate who He gave for our redemption. He gave His dear Son! It is surprising to learn that many Christians today do not believe that Jesus was the literal Son of God.
Jesus is God’s real son. God sent His Son. (John 3:17)
ANTICHRIST:
9. What does Antichrist deny so that the world can not see the love of the Father?
1 John 2:22
Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ?
He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son.
Note:

Denial of the true Father and Son constitutes an antichrist doctrine. Jesus is God’s Son, sent by the Father. Teachers who deny that Christ is God’s true Son present a different Christ, and a different Father than that of the Bible. Therefore, to deny the Father and His Son is a direct attack by the devil on the love of the Father!
SON OF GOD:
10. How does the Bible describe the person that does not believe on the true Son of God?
1 John 5:10
He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself:
he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son
Note:

John 3:16 tells us that God so loved the world that he gave His Son. John 3:17 tells us that God sent His Son. Our Father’s love for sinners is so strong that He gave His gentle Son. To deny God’s sacrifice in the gift of His Son is telling a lie about God’s love.
11. What must we confess if we are to have God dwelling in us?
1 John 4:15
Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God
Note:

The entire point of this study is to become sons and daughters of God. We cannot have this experience without first loving God. But we cannot love God until we first see something! We must first see that God loves us! It is then that our hearts respond, and we can have a trust response towards God.
GOD LOVES US:
12. Before we love God, what must we first see?
1 John 4:19
We love him,
because he first loved us
Note:
God’s love is displayed in the gift of Jesus. God so loved the world that He gave us His Son to die for our sins. As we start to see this love, our hearts respond with a responding chord.
13. How did God show His love for man?
1 John 4:10
Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.
Note
: We are beginning to see the most wonderful picture. Salvation is our response to the heart of God.
14. On what basis should we rely on God for our salvation?
1 John 4:16
And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us.
God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.
Note:
God not only loves us with an everlasting love, but God Himself
is
love. To trust in His love is to dwell in it. This is the secret to having God dwelling in us. He dwells in us as we relish His love for us and believe in His Son.
15. What does perfect love cast out?
1 John 4:17
Herein is our love made perfect
, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment… 18
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear:
because fear hath torment.
He that feareth is not made perfect in love
Note:
Fear is the result of sin. Because all of us have sinned, we are all victims of the fear of death. (See Hebrews 2:14, 15) Only God’s redeeming love can cast out this fear.
16. Does Paul say that there is anything that can separate us from the love of Christ?
Romans 8:35

Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? 36 As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. 37 Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us. 38
For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
PART 2:
CHRIST’S MINISTRY OF HEALING:
17. Where in the Bible does it say that Jesus healed?
Matthew 4:23
And Jesus went about all Galilee,
teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and
healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people
Note:
Jesus healed the people’s sickness and diseases.
18. When Jesus healed the paralytic, why did He say your sins be forgiven you?
Matthew 9:5
For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk?
But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins
, (then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.
Note:
Jesus told the paralytic that his sins be forgiven him. His supernatural healing power showed that He also had the power from God to forgive sins.
THE APOSTLES HEALED PEOPLE:
19. What power did Jesus give to His apostles?
Matthew 10:1
And when he had called unto him his
twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.
Note:
Jesus gave His disciples power to heal diseases.
20. What type of illnesses did the Apostles heal?
Blind:
Acts 9:17

And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest
receive thy sight,
and be filled with the Holy Ghost. 18
And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized
Paralyzed:
Acts 9:33
And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was
sick of the palsy.
34 And
Peter said unto him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately
Lame:
Acts 14:8
And there sat a certain man at Lystra,
impotent in his feet, being a cripple
from his mother’s womb, who never had walked: 9
The same heard Paul speak: who stedfastly beholding him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed,
Said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped and walked.
Unclean spirits:
Acts 16:16
And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel
possessed with a spirit of divination
met us, which brought her masters much gain by
soothsaying
: 17 The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation. 18 And this did she many days.
But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.
Even a man with severe diarrhea:
Acts 28:7

In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously. 8 And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay
sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
CHURCH ELDERS ANOINT WITH OIL:
21. What are we to be anointed with when we are sick?
James 5:14
Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:
Note:

When we are sick we are admonished to call for the elders and let them pray over us and anoint us with oil. God gave the apostles power to heal all manner of sickness. Today, we are to pray and anoint the sick in the name of the Lord.
22. What must we have besides prayer to heal the sick?
James 5:15
And
the prayer of faith shall save the sick
, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.
Note:

The prayer of faith shall save the sick. We must believe that Jesus heals the sick. We must have faith in His healing power. God heals us because he loves us. He also is showing us that Jesus has the power to forgive sins. We are all sinners and Christ forgives our sins when we have faith in Him.
CONFESS SINS ONE TO ANOTHER:
23. What brings us together as a body of believers?
James 5:16
Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.

The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much. 17 Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months.
Note:

We are to come together and pray for each other. We are also to confess our faults one to another. Often, new or immature believers will neglect confessing faults one to another. Instead, they will judge each other’s character and motives. This is not God’s way. God’s way is to be our brother’s keeper. We are to love one another and pray fervently one for another. When we bite at each other we show that we are still carnal and forget that we are all brethren and that we are all in this together.
24. What shows that we are carnal and not spiritual?
1 Corinthians 3:3
For ye are yet carnal: for whereas there is among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are ye not carnal, and walk as men
Note:
We can tell when we are still carnal. We can know that we are walking in our old flesh when we feel like we are not being treated fairly. We then bite at each other causing divisions and strife.
25. What are you building your foundation upon?
1 Corinthians 3:12
Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble;
13 Every man’s work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because
it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man’s work of what sort it is
If any man’s work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward
Note
: Let us confess our faults to each other so that we can be healed.
Our foundation will be revealed when it is tried by affliction (fire). If we build our foundation on wood, hay, or stubble it will be burned up when affliction comes.
When we build our life’s character upon feelings instead of upon the higher calling of the love of God, we are building upon wood, hay, or stubble.
When we build our foundation upon the love of God, we are building upon gold, silver, and precious stones. (See Galatians 5:6)
As we confess our faults one to one another in humility, let us behold the love of Christ. We will then be changed into His image, from glory to glory. (See 2 Corinthians 3:18)
